Informed Consent Form for Participation in Research

What is the purpose of this study?

You are being invited to participate in a research study. The purpose of the study is to better understand how recommenders make their recommendation decisions and how audiences respond to recommendations.

What will happen if I agree to participate?

    If you agree to participate, you will be asked to make multiple decisions between two candidates. All decisions involve making a prediction between which of two candidates you expect to perform better on a task. You will also be shown the recommendation made by a prior participant in the study. You can choose to follow their recommendations or not.
    You will be paid $1.20 for your participation in the study, with the opportunity to earn up to a $2 bonus.
    Your bonus payment will depend the outcome of one of the decisions you make in the study (randomly drawn).
    The study should take 6 minutes to complete.
    All measures will be completed online.

How do I know if I’m eligible to participate?

Participants must be 18 or older and located in the US at the time of participation.

Are there any possible risks to participation?

There is a potential risk of a breach of confidentiality, meaning that someone who is not part of the research team may gain access to your data. We will do our best to keep information about you private and confidential by keeping the research records in a secure location and transferring them securely if they are shared with others, but we cannot reduce the risk to zero.

There may be other risks to participation in this research that are not known at this time. If additional risks are identified during your participation in the research, you will be informed so that you may decide whether or not to continue your participation.

What are the expected, possible benefits of the research?

There are no direct benefits to you if you agree to participate in this study.

If your data are shared with others for future research, you will not receive any direct benefit from that research. However, sharing your data may contribute to research that could help others in the future.

Will I receive any compensation if I participate?

You will receive $1.20 for participating in the study, with the opportunity to earn up to $2 more.

You will not receive any financial benefit from or ownership in any products or data generated as a result of this research.

Will it cost me anything to participate?

This research study is not expected to result in any costs to you for your normal participation. CMU will not reimburse you for any additional costs that you may incur from participating in this research or for medical treatment if you become injured or ill while participating in the research.

What will happen to my research data in the future after the research is over?

Carnegie Mellon University researchers and their collaborators in this research may use the data collected in this study for future research purposes and may share the data with others for future research or commercial purposes. Sharing data is a common part of research and may increase what we can learn from your participation in the study. Often, data sharing is required as a condition of funding or for publishing study results. It is also needed to allow other researchers to validate our study findings and to come up with new ideas.

Your data may be shared with researchers at CMU and other institutions, for-profit companies, the study’s sponsors, government agencies, and other partners for future, unknown research or commercial purposes. Your data may also be placed in government or other public databases and repositories to be used by others for their own research. We would use and share your data without getting additional informed consent from you.

Any information that can easily identify you will be removed from the data prior to sharing with others or prior to use in our future research or commercial development.

If you do not want your data to be used for our future research or commercial development or shared with others, you should not participate in this study.

How will my information be kept confidential?

Your data will be shared within the research team, which consists of Dr. Rosalind Chow (Carnegie Mellon University), Jose Cervantez (doctoral student at University of Pennsylvania), and Dr. Erika Kirgios (University of Chicago). Data will be stored on password protected devices and/or data-sharing platforms (e.g., Drive, iCloud, Box, etc.)

By participating in the study, you understand and agree that Carnegie Mellon University may be required to disclose your consent form, data and other personally identifiable information as required by law, regulation, subpoena or court order. As part of their responsibilities for human subjects protection oversight of the study and for data security purposes, select Carnegie Mellon University staff or consultants may also have access to your research data for compliance, auditing, or operations purposes. Additionally, your data may be shared with government agencies that have oversight of the study or to whom access is required under the law such as the Office of Human Research Protections (OHRP).

Collaborators – This research is being done in collaboration with Jose Cervantez (doctoral student at University of Pennsylvania), and Dr. Erika Kirgios (University of Chicago).

Vendors or other non-CMU owned software, services, products, or devices used in the research – Data is collected through Qualtrics, a survey platform. This company is not owned by CMU. The company will have access to the research data that you produce and any identifiable information that is shared with them while using their product. Please note that Carnegie Mellon does not control the Terms and Conditions of the company or how they will use or protect any information that they collect.

Your data may also need to be shared with other companies or organizations that are unknown at this time. The data will be shared only for the purposes of completing the research described in this consent form. Examples of these purposes include transcribing recordings or conducting data analysis.

Otherwise, your confidentiality will be maintained in the following manner:

Your data and consent form will be kept separate. Your research data will be stored in a secure location on CMU property or via secure electronic means and in the control of CMU and/or the above-named collaborators or vendors in this research. By participating in the research, you understand and agree that the data and information gathered during this study may be used by Carnegie Mellon and its collaborators and published and/or disclosed by Carnegie Mellon to others outside of Carnegie Mellon as described above. All research data will be kept by CMU for a minimum of 3 years.

Any original data files will be stored in a secured location accessed only by authorized individuals.

What are my rights as a research participant?

Your participation is voluntary. You are free to stop your participation at any point. Refusal to participate, withdrawal of your consent, or discontinued participation in the study will not result in any penalty or loss of benefits or rights to which you might otherwise be entitled. If you decide to withdraw your consent or otherwise discontinue your participation, any data that have already been collected may still be used in the research. Any data that have already been shared with others may not be able to be recalled. The Principal Investigator may, at their discretion, remove you from the study for any reason including adverse events that you experienced, your safety, your ineligibility for the research, or your failure to perform research activities as requested. The research itself may also be terminated at any time.

What if I have questions? Who can I contact?

If you have any questions about this study, you should ask them now or you can also ask questions at any time in the future. If you have questions later, desire additional information, or wish to stop your participation please contact the Principal Investigator by mail, phone, or e-mail using the contact information listed on the first page of this consent. Please note that if your data has been de-identified or collected anonymously, it cannot be withdrawn from the research because we will not be able to determine what data belongs to you.

If you have questions pertaining to your rights as a research participant or to report concerns about this study, you should contact the Institutional Review Board (IRB) of Carnegie Mellon University. Email: irb-review@andrew.cmu.edu Phone: 412-268-4721.

Voluntary Consent

You should print a copy of this consent form for your records. You are encouraged to ask any questions that you have about the research now or in the future.

Informed Consent Form for Participation in Research

What is the purpose of this study?

You are being invited to participate in a research study. The purpose of the study is to better understand how recommenders make their recommendation decisions and how audiences respond to recommendations.

What will happen if I agree to participate?

  • If you agree to participate, you will be asked to make multiple decisions between two candidates. All decisions involve making a prediction between which of two candidates you expect to perform better on a task. You will also be shown the recommendation made by a prior participant in the study. You can choose to follow their recommendations or not.
  • You will be paid $1.20 for your participation in the study, with the opportunity to earn up to a $2 bonus.
  • Your bonus payment will depend the outcome of one of the decisions you make in the study (randomly drawn).
  • The study should take 6 minutes to complete.
  • All measures will be completed online.

How do I know if I’m eligible to participate?

Participants must be 18 or older and located in the US at the time of participation.

Are there any possible risks to participation?

There is a potential risk of a breach of confidentiality, meaning that someone who is not part of the research team may gain access to your data. We will do our best to keep information about you private and confidential by keeping the research records in a secure location and transferring them securely if they are shared with others, but we cannot reduce the risk to zero.

There may be other risks to participation in this research that are not known at this time. If additional risks are identified during your participation in the research, you will be informed so that you may decide whether or not to continue your participation.

What are the expected, possible benefits of the research?

There are no direct benefits to you if you agree to participate in this study.

If your data are shared with others for future research, you will not receive any direct benefit from that research. However, sharing your data may contribute to research that could help others in the future.

Will I receive any compensation if I participate?

You will receive $1.20 for participating in the study, with the opportunity to earn up to $2 more.

You will not receive any financial benefit from or ownership in any products or data generated as a result of this research.

Will it cost me anything to participate?

This research study is not expected to result in any costs to you for your normal participation. CMU will not reimburse you for any additional costs that you may incur from participating in this research or for medical treatment if you become injured or ill while participating in the research.

What will happen to my research data in the future after the research is over?

Carnegie Mellon University researchers and their collaborators in this research may use the data collected in this study for future research purposes and may share the data with others for future research or commercial purposes. Sharing data is a common part of research and may increase what we can learn from your participation in the study. Often, data sharing is required as a condition of funding or for publishing study results. It is also needed to allow other researchers to validate our study findings and to come up with new ideas.

Your data may be shared with researchers at CMU and other institutions, for-profit companies, the study’s sponsors, government agencies, and other partners for future, unknown research or commercial purposes. Your data may also be placed in government or other public databases and repositories to be used by others for their own research. We would use and share your data without getting additional informed consent from you.

Any information that can easily identify you will be removed from the data prior to sharing with others or prior to use in our future research or commercial development.

If you do not want your data to be used for our future research or commercial development or shared with others, you should not participate in this study.

How will my information be kept confidential?

Your data will be shared within the research team, which consists of Dr. Rosalind Chow (Carnegie Mellon University), Jose Cervantez (doctoral student at University of Pennsylvania), and Dr. Erika Kirgios (University of Chicago). Data will be stored on password protected devices and/or data-sharing platforms (e.g., Drive, iCloud, Box, etc.)

Additionally, your data may be shared with government agencies that have oversight of the study or to whom access is required under the law such as the Office of Human Research Protections (OHRP).

The company will have access to the research data that you produce and any identifiable information that is shared with them while using their product. Please note that Carnegie Mellon does not control the Terms and Conditions of the company or how they will use or protect any information that they collect.

Your data may also need to be shared with other companies or organizations that are unknown at this time. The data will be shared only for the purposes of completing the research described in this consent form. Examples of these purposes include transcribing recordings or conducting data analysis.

Otherwise, your confidentiality will be maintained in the following manner:

Your data and consent form will be kept separate. Your research data will be stored in a secure location on CMU property or via secure electronic means and in the control of CMU and/or the above-named collaborators or vendors in this research. By participating in the research, you understand and agree that the data and information gathered during this study may be used by Carnegie Mellon and its collaborators and published and/or disclosed by Carnegie Mellon to others outside of Carnegie Mellon as described above. Any original data files will be stored in a secured location accessed only by authorized individuals.

Your participation is voluntary. You are free to stop your participation at any point. If you decide to withdraw your consent or otherwise discontinue your participation, any data that have already been collected may still be used in the research. Any data that have already been shared with others may not be able to be recalled. The Principal Investigator may, at their discretion, remove you from the study for any reason including adverse events that you experienced, your safety, your ineligibility for the research, or your failure to perform research activities as requested. The research itself may also be terminated at any time.

What if I have questions? Who can I contact?

If you have any questions about this study, you should ask them now or you can also ask questions at any time in the future. If you have questions later, desire additional information, or wish to stop your participation please contact the Principal Investigator by mail, phone, or e-mail using the contact information listed on the first page of this consent. Please note that if your data has been de-identified or collected anonymously, it cannot be withdrawn from the research because we will not be able to determine what data belongs to you.

Voluntary Consent
